    1|       |//! In-chat approval prompts for supervised tool calls.
    2|       |//!
    3|       |//! When a host parks a tool call for approval, the user who started the turn
    4|       |//! must be asked in the chat the turn came from, and their `yes`/`no` reply
    5|       |//! routed back. [`ApprovalSurface`] owns the channel half of that:
    6|       |//!
    7|       |//! 1. [`ApprovalSurface::record_inbound`] remembers where each conversation's
    8|       |//!    last message came from (reply target and thread).
    9|       |//! 2. [`ApprovalSurface::surface`] sends the prompt back to that chat.
   10|       |//!
   11|       |//! The approval decision itself (parking, TTL, parsing the reply) stays with
   12|       |//! the host. Only channels whose capabilities set `chat_approvals` take part.
   13|       |
   14|       |use std::collections::HashMap;
   15|       |use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};
   16|       |
   17|       |use crate::capabilities::capabilities_for;
   18|       |use crate::context::conversation_history_key_parts;
   19|       |use crate::traits::{Channel, ChannelSendExt, SendMessage};
   20|       |
   21|       |const LOG_PREFIX: &str = "[channel-approval]";
   22|       |
   23|       |/// Render an approval request as a chat message.
   24|      7|pub fn format_approval_prompt(tool_name: &str, action_summary: &str) -> String {
   25|      7|    format!(
   26|       |        "🔐 Approval needed\nTool: `{tool_name}`\nAction: {action_summary}\n\nReply `yes` to approve or `no` to deny."
   27|       |    )
   28|      7|}
   29|       |

   40|       |    pub request_id: String,
   41|       |    pub tool_name: String,
   42|       |    pub action_summary: String,

   48|       |
   49|       |/// What [`ApprovalSurface::surface`] did.
   50|       |#[derive(Debug)]
   51|       |pub enum SurfaceOutcome {
   52|       |    /// The prompt was sent.
   53|       |    Sent,
   54|       |    /// The channel has no in-chat approval capability.
   55|       |    Unsupported,
   56|       |    /// No inbound message was recorded for this conversation, so there is
   57|       |    /// nowhere to send the prompt. The parked call will time out denied.
   58|       |    NoReplyContext,
   59|       |    /// The channel is not running in this runtime.
   60|       |    ChannelNotRegistered,
   61|       |    /// Sending failed.
   62|       |    SendFailed(anyhow::Error),
   63|       |}

    2|       |//!
    3|       |//! Whether the edit route exists is a property of the deployed backend, not of

   12|       |
   13|       |/// Provider key for the latch: inbound channels arrive provider-prefixed
   14|       |/// (`telegram:<chat>`) and route existence is per provider.

   16|     32|    channel.split(':').next().unwrap_or(channel).to_string()
   17|     32|}

   19|       |/// `true` once this process has learned the backend serves no edit route for

   22|     25|    EDIT_UNSUPPORTED_PROVIDERS
   23|     25|        .get_or_init(Default::default)
   24|     25|        .lock()
   25|     25|        .map(|set| set.contains(&edit_capability_key(channel)))
   26|     25|        .unwrap_or(false)
   27|     25|}
   28|       |

   32|      5|    if let Ok(mut set) = EDIT_UNSUPPORTED_PROVIDERS

   34|      5|        .lock()

    1|       |//! Progressive reply delivery over a message-relay backend.
    2|       |//!
    3|       |//! While an agent turn runs, a chat user should see activity: a typing
    4|       |//! indicator, an evolving draft of the reply, an ephemeral "💭 Thinking:"
    5|       |//! bubble, and a rotating "still working" filler during long turns. When the
    6|       |//! turn ends, the canonical reply replaces the draft and every ephemeral
    7|       |//! bubble is deleted.
    8|       |//!
    9|       |//! This module owns that choreography: the timing, the per-turn state, the
   10|       |//! edit/delete/typing failure latches, and the finalize invariants (never post
   11|       |//! a duplicate bubble, never leave a stale draft on screen). The host supplies
   12|       |//! the transport as a [`ProgressiveSender`]; OpenHuman implements it over its
   13|       |//! backend REST relay.

    1|       |//! Construct the configured provider set from a [`ChannelsConfig`].
    2|       |//!
    3|       |//! This is the portable half of channel startup: read config, build providers.
    4|       |//! It lives here rather than in a host because it is the same for every host —
    5|       |//! and because a second copy is how the two drift. The module
    6|       |//! (`tinychannels-module`) and the OpenHuman desktop core both call it.
    7|       |//!
    8|       |//! # What this function deliberately does NOT do
    9|       |//!
   10|       |//! Three things in channel startup are host policy and stay with the caller:
   11|       |//!
   12|       |//! - **Credential hydration.** Secrets may live in a keyring, an environment
   13|       |//!   variable or the config file, and only the host knows which. Hydrate
   14|       |//!   `config` *before* calling this — a provider whose token is still a
   15|       |//!   placeholder is built here without complaint, because this function cannot
   16|       |//!   tell a deliberately-empty token from an unresolved one.
   17|       |//! - **HTTP transport.** Proxy configuration, TLS backend and timeouts belong to
   18|       |//!   the host's runtime, so they arrive as a [`HttpClientFactory`].
   19|       |//! - **Host capabilities.** Speech-to-text, the persisted allowlist, the event
   20|       |//!   sink and the lifecycle hook come from [`ChannelHost`], which a host
   21|       |//!   implements. [`NoopHost`](crate::NoopHost) is the correct argument when
   22|       |//!   there are none; each capability is optional and every provider degrades
   23|       |//!   rather than failing without one.
   24|       |//!
   25|       |//! # Misconfiguration warns, it does not fail
   26|       |//!
   27|       |//! A provider whose config is present but unusable (WhatsApp with neither a
   28|       |//! Cloud nor a Web shape, Yuanbao with an invalid secret) is logged and skipped.
   29|       |//! Returning a `Result` would mean one bad stanza takes down every other
   30|       |//! channel, which is the wrong trade for a long-running messaging surface.
   31|       |

    1|       |//! The **host boundary**: one generic capability surface every channel
    2|       |//! provider can lean on, standardized across lean and rich providers alike.
    3|       |//!
    4|       |//! ## Why
    5|       |//!
    6|       |//! [`crate::traits::Channel`] covers the *transport* side of a provider —
    7|       |//! receive inbound messages, send outbound ones. That is all a **lean**
    8|       |//! provider (irc, signal, slack) needs. **Rich** providers (web, telegram,
    9|       |//! presentation, whatsapp_web) additionally need to reach back into the host
   10|       |//! runtime: run an agent turn, transcribe a voice note, park an approval,
   11|       |//! recall conversation history, publish domain events, register shutdown, or
   12|       |//! record telemetry.
   13|       |//!
   14|       |//! Historically those providers called OpenHuman internals directly, which is
   15|       |//! exactly why they could not be ported into TinyChannels. [`ChannelHost`]
   16|       |//! inverts that dependency: the **host** implements a set of small, portable
   17|       |//! capability traits, and providers consume them through one aggregator that
   18|       |//! is handed to them at construction via [`ProviderContext`].
   19|       |//!
   20|       |//! ## Shape
   21|       |//!
   22|       |//! - Each capability is an independent object-safe trait ([`TurnDispatcher`],
   23|       |//!   [`Transcriber`], [`SpeechSynthesizer`], [`ApprovalGate`], [`ReactionGate`],
   24|       |//!   [`ConversationStore`], [`EventSink`], [`LifecycleRegistry`], [`RunLedger`],
   25|       |//!   plus the pre-existing [`crate::context::Memory`]).
   26|       |//! - [`ChannelHost`] exposes each as an `Option<Arc<dyn …>>` accessor that
   27|       |//!   defaults to `None`. A host implements only what it can back; a provider
   28|       |//!   asks only for what it needs and degrades gracefully when a capability is
   29|       |//!   absent.
   30|       |//! - [`HostCapabilities`] is a cheap, copyable descriptor a provider can check
   31|       |//!   up front (e.g. "only advertise voice replies if `host.capabilities().tts`").
   32|       |//! - [`ChannelHostBuilder`] composes a concrete host from whatever capabilities
   33|       |//!   you have; [`NoopHost`] is the empty host for lean providers and tests.
   34|       |//!
   35|       |//! A provider that uses **none** of this keeps working unchanged — it just
   36|       |//! ignores the `host` on its [`ProviderContext`].
   37|       |
   38|       |mod dispatch;
   39|       |mod noop;
   40|       |mod services;
   41|       |

   20|       |/// Format a non-2xx response from the Discord REST API as a string
   21|       |/// suitable for a JSON-RPC error result.
   22|       |///
   23|       |/// **Load-bearing for issue #2285**: the global JSON-RPC dispatcher
   24|       |/// at `src/core/jsonrpc.rs::is_session_expired_error` matches any
   25|       |/// error string that contains `"401"` AND `"unauthorized"` as a
   26|       |/// signal that the OpenHuman backend session has expired, and
   27|       |/// publishes a `DomainEvent::SessionExpired` event that signs the
   28|       |/// user out. A raw upstream Discord 401 (revoked bot token) would
   29|       |/// previously trip that classifier — opening the connected-Discord
   30|       |/// card on the Channels page logged the user out of OpenHuman over
   31|       |/// a *Discord* credentials problem.
   32|       |///
   33|       |/// The fix is to convert auth failures here into a Discord-domain
   34|       |/// message that:
   35|       |///
   36|       |///  1. Does NOT contain both `"401"` and `"unauthorized"` as a pair
   37|       |///     (so the global classifier ignores it).
   38|       |///  2. Tells the user the actual remediation: rotate the bot token
   39|       |///     at `Settings → Channels → Discord`.
   40|       |///  3. Preserves the originating endpoint identifier in the message
   41|       |///     so triage can still see WHICH Discord call failed without
   42|       |///     plumbing a separate error code.
   43|       |///
   44|       |/// Other non-2xx statuses (400 / 404 / 5xx) pass through with a
   45|       |/// `Discord API error` prefix — they don't match the
   46|       |/// `is_session_expired_error` predicate even when verbatim.
   47|      4|fn format_discord_http_error(endpoint: &str, status: reqwest::StatusCode, body: &str) -> String {
   48|      4|    if status == reqwest::StatusCode::UNAUTHORIZED || status == reqwest::StatusCode::FORBIDDEN {
                                                                    ^2
   49|      3|        let kind = if status == reqwest::StatusCode::UNAUTHORIZED {
   50|      2|            "bot token was rejected"
   51|       |        } else {
   52|      1|            "bot token lacks required Discord permissions"
   53|       |        };
   54|       |        // Spell out the HTTP code so `lower.contains("401")` does NOT
   55|       |        // match — see #2285 rationale on this helper. Also avoid the
   56|       |        // word `unauthorized` for the same reason; "rejected"/"forbidden"
   57|       |        // are the user-visible equivalents.
   58|      3|        let code_word = if status == reqwest::StatusCode::UNAUTHORIZED {
   59|      2|            "four-oh-one"
   60|       |        } else {
   61|      1|            "four-oh-three"
   62|       |        };
   63|       |        // Deliberately do NOT splice the upstream body into this
   64|       |        // user-facing message — Discord's auth-error bodies often
   65|       |        // include the literal words "401" and "Unauthorized", which
   66|       |        // would smuggle the cascade trigger back in. The body is
   67|       |        // still in `tracing::debug!` logs above the call site for
   68|       |        // triage; the user-facing message only needs the remediation.
   69|      3|        let _ = body;
   70|      3|        format!(
   71|       |            "Discord {endpoint}: {kind} (upstream HTTP {code_word}). \
   72|       |             Open Settings → Channels → Discord and rotate / reconnect the bot \
   73|       |             token."
   74|       |        )
   75|       |    } else {
   76|      1|        format!("Discord {endpoint} failed ({status}): {body}")
   77|       |    }

    1|       |//! WhatsApp Web channel backed by upstream [`whatsapp-rust`] 0.7.
    2|       |//!
    3|       |//! # Why the upgrade
    4|       |//!
    5|       |//! The previous implementation used `wa-rs` 0.2 (a fork that pinned to stable
    6|       |//! Rust). That fork silently dropped `Event::Message` for LID-addressed
    7|       |//! contacts and group sender-key (`skmsg`) messages: the protocol layer
    8|       |//! decrypted the payload but never dispatched it to user code, breaking
    9|       |//! agent dispatch for the bulk of modern WhatsApp traffic (LID is the
   10|       |//! current default). Upstream `whatsapp-rust` fixed this in PRs #170
   11|       |//! (SKDM tracking) + #181 (LID/PN mapping) + sender-key dispatch.
   12|       |//!
   13|       |//! # Feature Flag
   14|       |//!
   15|       |//! ```sh
   16|       |//! cargo build --features whatsapp-web
   17|       |//! ```
   18|       |//!
   19|       |//! # Configuration
   20|       |//!
   21|       |//! ```toml
   22|       |//! [channels.whatsapp]
   23|       |//! session_path = "~/.openhuman/whatsapp-session.db"  # Reserved for durable Web mode
   24|       |//! pair_phone = "15551234567"                         # Optional: pair-code linking
   25|       |//! allowed_numbers = ["+1234567890", "*"]             # Same shape as Cloud API
   26|       |//! ```
   27|       |//!
   28|       |//! # Runtime negotiation
   29|       |//!
   30|       |//! Selected automatically by the channels runtime startup when `session_path`
   31|       |//! is set. The Cloud API channel ([`super::whatsapp`]) is used when
   32|       |//! `phone_number_id` is set instead.
   33|       |//!
   34|       |//! # Migration note
   35|       |//!
   36|       |//! The upstream `sqlite-storage` feature currently uses Diesel, whose
   37|       |//! native sqlite binding conflicts with the TinyAgents 1.3 / rusqlite 0.40
   38|       |//! baseline. Until OpenHuman owns a rusqlite-backed durable store for the
   39|       |//! WhatsApp backend traits, this channel uses wacore's in-memory backend and
   40|       |//! requires re-linking after restart.
   41|       |//!
   42|       |//! [`whatsapp-rust`]: https://docs.rs/whatsapp-rust/0.7

/home/enamakel/work/openhuman/vendor/tinychannels/worktrees/cov-discord/src/providers/yuanbao/ids.rs:
    1|       |//! Account-id shortening for yuanbao.
    2|       |//!
    3|       |//! Yuanbao uids (`from_account`) are 64-char hashes assigned by the platform.
    4|       |//! The composite `ChannelMessage` thread_id that downstream consumers derive
    5|       |//! from `sender` and `reply_target` (`channel:yuanbao_<sender>_<reply_target>`)
    6|       |//! becomes ~145 chars. After the conversation store hex-encodes that for the
    7|       |//! per-thread JSONL filename it grows to ~296 chars, exceeding `NAME_MAX`
    8|       |//! (255 bytes) on ext4/HFS+/APFS/NTFS — writes fail with `ENAMETOOLONG` and
    9|       |//! channel history is lost.
   10|       |//!
   11|       |//! Rather than push the filesystem limit into shared `ConversationStore` code,
   12|       |//! we shorten yuanbao-specific ids at the channel boundary. Internal yuanbao
   13|       |//! state (echo guard, access control, owner-command check) keeps the original
   14|       |//! `from_account` — only the value emitted on `ChannelMessage.sender` /
   15|       |//! `ChannelMessage.reply_target` is shortened.
   16|       |//!
   17|       |//! Format: `<first 8 chars of uid>_<first 16 hex chars of sha256(uid)>`.
   18|       |//! The 8-char prefix keeps logs roughly groupable for the same user; the
   19|       |//! sha256 suffix guarantees uniqueness across uids that share a prefix.
   20|       |
   21|       |use sha2::{Digest, Sha256};
   22|       |
   23|       |/// Max raw account-id length before the shortening kicks in.
   24|       |///
   25|       |/// Anything shorter is passed through unchanged so short upstream-style ids
   26|       |/// (e.g. numeric ids, future protocol changes) keep their natural form.
   27|       |const ACCOUNT_ID_PASSTHROUGH_MAX: usize = 24;
   28|       |
   29|       |/// Shorten a yuanbao account id for use in `ChannelMessage.sender` /
   30|       |/// `ChannelMessage.reply_target`. See module docs for rationale.
   31|     21|pub(super) fn shorten_account_id(uid: &str) -> String {
   32|     21|    if uid.len() <= ACCOUNT_ID_PASSTHROUGH_MAX {
   33|     10|        return uid.to_string();
   34|     11|    }
   35|     11|    let prefix: String = uid.chars().take(8).collect();
   36|     11|    let digest = hex::encode(Sha256::digest(uid.as_bytes()));
   37|     11|    format!("{prefix}_{}", &digest[..16])
   38|     21|}
   39|       |
   40|       |/// Shorten a yuanbao `reply_target`, preserving the `g:<group_code>` shape
   41|       |/// used for group chats. The `g:` discriminator is required by outbound
   42|       |/// routing (see [`super::types::InboundContext::reply_target`]).
   43|      7|pub(super) fn shorten_reply_target(reply_target: &str) -> String {
   44|      7|    if let Some(group_code) = reply_target.strip_prefix("g:") {
                              ^3
   45|      3|        format!("g:{}", shorten_account_id(group_code))
   46|       |    } else {
   47|      4|        shorten_account_id(reply_target)
   48|       |    }
   49|      7|}

  465|       |    /// Decode a biz push body, run it through every stage, return the outcome.
  466|       |    ///
  467|       |    /// The yuanbao gateway may push the biz body as either protobuf
  468|       |    /// (`InboundMessagePush`) or a JSON string with the same field shape
  469|       |    /// (snake_case + `log_ext.trace_id`). We sniff the first non-whitespace
  470|       |    /// byte to pick the decoder — `{` means JSON, anything else is treated
  471|       |    /// as protobuf. Mirrors plugin gateway.ts::wsPushToInboundMessage
  472|       |    /// (l. 288), which tries protobuf first and falls back to JSON.
  473|      8|    pub async fn process(&self, biz_body: &[u8]) -> PipelineOutcome {
  474|      8|        let is_json = biz_body
  475|      8|            .iter()
  476|      8|            .find(|b| !b.is_ascii_whitespace())
  477|      8|            .map(|b| *b == b'{')
  478|      8|            .unwrap_or(false);
  479|       |
  480|      8|        let msg = if is_json {
                          ^6
  481|      3|            match decode_inbound_json(biz_body) {
  482|      2|                Ok(m) => m,
  483|      1|                Err(e) => return PipelineOutcome::Failed(e),
  484|       |            }
  485|       |        } else {
  486|      5|            match decode_inbound_push(biz_body) {
  487|      4|                Ok(m) => m,
  488|      1|                Err(e) => return PipelineOutcome::Failed(e),
  489|       |            }
  490|       |        };
  491|      6|        let mut ctx = PipelineCtx {
  492|      6|            msg,
  493|      6|            source: Source::default(),
  494|      6|            text: String::new(),
  495|      6|            image_urls: Vec::new(),
  496|      6|            is_at_bot: false,
  497|      6|            is_owner_command: false,
  498|      6|            kind: MessageKind::Text,
  499|      6|        };
  500|     73|        for stage in &self.stages {
                                   ^6
  501|     73|            match stage.process(&self.state, &mut ctx).await {
  502|       |                MwResult::Continue => {
  503|     71|                    trace!("[yuanbao:inbound] {} pass", stage.name());
                                                                      ^0    ^0
  504|       |                }
  505|      1|                MwResult::Skip(reason) => {
  506|      1|                    debug!("[yuanbao:inbound] {} filtered ({})", stage.name(), reason);
                                                                               ^0    ^0
  507|      1|                    return PipelineOutcome::Filtered(reason);
  508|       |                }
  509|      1|                MwResult::Abort(err) => return PipelineOutcome::Failed(err),
  510|       |            }
  511|       |        }
  512|      4|        PipelineOutcome::Dispatch(ctx)
  513|      8|    }

    1|       |//! Yuanbao WebSocket ConnMsg envelope + built-in protocol commands
    2|       |//! (auth-bind, ping, push-ack) + TIM `MsgBodyElement` codecs.
    3|       |//!
    4|       |//! Each WebSocket binary frame carries one full `ConnMsg` protobuf
    5|       |//! message; **no extra length prefix is needed** (the WS frame boundary
    6|       |//! delimits one message). Verified against the hermes-agent Python
    7|       |//! reference (yuanbao_proto.py) and the TypeScript openclaw plugin.
    8|       |//!
    9|       |//! Business-layer codecs (send-message / heartbeat / group query) live
   10|       |//! in [`super::proto_biz`]. Wire-format primitives (varint, FieldValue,
   11|       |//! parse_fields) live in [`super::wire`].
   12|       |
   13|       |use super::errors::YuanbaoError;
   14|       |use super::proto_constants::*;
   15|       |use super::types::*;
   16|       |use super::wire::{
   17|       |    FieldValue, encode_field_bytes, encode_field_string, encode_field_varint, get_bytes,
   18|       |    get_repeated_bytes, get_string, get_varint, next_seq_no, parse_fields,
   19|       |};
   20|       |
   21|       |// Re-export wire primitives for downstream callers (tests, tools).
   22|       |pub use super::wire::{decode_varint, encode_varint};
   23|       |
   24|       |// ─── ConnMsg envelope ──────────────────────────────────────────────
   25|       |//
   26|       |//   message Head {
   27|       |//     uint32 cmd_type = 1;
   28|       |//     string cmd      = 2;
   29|       |//     uint32 seq_no   = 3;
   30|       |//     string msg_id   = 4;
   31|       |//     string module   = 5;
   32|       |//     bool   need_ack = 6;
   33|       |//     int32  status   = 10;

    1|       |//! Module-side runtime for trusted tinybus `cdylib` integrations.
    2|       |//!
    3|       |//! Each module owns a Tokio runtime. A statically linked `cdylib` has its own
    4|       |//! Tokio thread-locals, so attempting to borrow the host runtime is both
    5|       |//! incorrect and capable of silently blocking a host worker thread.
    6|       |//!
    7|       |//! Caller context depends on the trusted host's optional ABI-v1 routing callback.
    8|       |//! Its assertion is captured per frame at enqueue time; older host prefixes
    9|       |//! remain compatible but supply unverified context. Sender headers remain intact
   10|       |//! for protocol routing and streams even when they carry no caller authority.

  258|       |// Private envelope captures trusted-host routing before the frame is queued.
  259|       |type IncomingFrame = (Vec<u8>, bool);
  260|       |
  261|       |struct ModuleTransport {
  262|       |    host: HostCalls,
  263|       |    inbound: Mutex<mpsc::Receiver<IncomingFrame>>,
  264|       |    provenance: Arc<AtomicBool>,
  265|       |    detach_on_panic: bool,
  266|       |}
  267|       |
  268|       |#[async_trait]
  269|       |impl Transport for ModuleTransport {
  270|       |    async fn send(&self, message: Message) -> Result<()> {
  271|       |        let panicked = message.header.error_name.as_deref() == Some(MODULE_PANIC_ERROR);
  272|       |        let bytes = serde_json::to_vec(&message)?;
  273|       |        if bytes.len() > MAX_FRAME_LEN {
  274|       |            return Err(Error::protocol("module frame exceeds the size cap"));
  275|       |        }
  276|       |        match self.host.send(&bytes) {
  277|       |            TB_OK => {
  278|       |                if panicked && self.detach_on_panic {
  279|       |                    self.host.fault();
  280|       |                }
  281|       |                Ok(())
  282|       |            }
  283|       |            TB_BACKPRESSURE => Err(Error::Backpressure),
  284|       |            TB_CLOSED => Err(Error::ConnectionClosed),
  285|       |            _ => Err(Error::transport("module host refused a frame")),
  286|       |        }
  287|       |    }
  288|       |
  289|       |    async fn recv(&self) -> Result<Option<Message>> {
  290|       |        let bytes = self.inbound.lock().await.recv().await;
  291|       |        let Some((bytes, brokered)) = bytes else {
  292|       |            return Ok(None);
  293|       |        };
  294|       |        self.host.wake();
  295|       |        let message = serde_json::from_slice(&bytes)?;
  296|       |        // The connection is the only reader and samples this slot immediately
  297|       |        // after recv. Keep header identity intact for stream ownership/routing;
  298|       |        // only contextual dispatch consumes the captured delivery authority.
  299|       |        self.provenance.store(brokered, Ordering::Release);
  300|       |        Ok(Some(message))
  301|       |    }
  302|       |
  303|       |    async fn close(&self) -> Result<()> {
  304|       |        self.inbound.lock().await.close();
  305|       |        Ok(())
  306|       |    }
  307|       |
  308|       |    fn describe(&self) -> String {
  309|       |        "module".to_string()
  310|       |    }
  311|       |}
  312|       |
  313|       |fn module_connection(transport: Arc<ModuleTransport>) -> Connection {
  314|       |    if transport.host.0.broker_routing.is_some() {
  315|       |        let provenance = transport.provenance.clone();
  316|       |        // SAFETY: this private transport has one reader, publishes the queue's
  317|       |        // per-frame proof before returning, and no other writer touches its
  318|       |        // slot. The trusted host asserts routing at deliver, not at receive.
  319|       |        unsafe { Connection::__attach_module_with_provenance(transport, provenance) }
  320|       |    } else {
  321|       |        Connection::attach(transport)
  322|       |    }
  323|       |}

  325|       |struct RuntimeState {
  326|       |    inbound: StdMutex<Option<mpsc::Sender<IncomingFrame>>>,
  327|       |    host: HostCalls,
  328|       |    runtime: StdMutex<Option<tokio::runtime::Runtime>>,
  329|       |    reinitialize: Option<Reinitialize>,
  330|       |}
  331|       |
  332|       |type Reinitialize = Box<dyn Fn(*const u8, usize) -> i32 + Send + Sync>;
  333|       |type ReinitializeFactory = Box<
  334|       |    dyn FnOnce(tokio::runtime::Handle, Arc<StdMutex<Option<Connection>>>) -> Reinitialize + Send,
  335|       |>;
  336|       |
  337|       |unsafe extern "C" fn deliver(ctx: *mut c_void, ptr: *const u8, len: usize) -> i32 {
  338|       |    match catch_unwind(AssertUnwindSafe(|| {
  339|       |        if ctx.is_null() || ptr.is_null() || len > MAX_FRAME_LEN {
  340|       |            return TB_BAD_ARGUMENT;
  341|       |        }
  342|       |        let state = unsafe { &*(ctx.cast::<RuntimeState>()) };
  343|       |        let brokered = state.host.is_broker_routed();
  344|       |        let bytes = unsafe { std::slice::from_raw_parts(ptr, len) }.to_vec();
  345|       |        let sender = state.inbound.lock().expect("module inbound lock").clone();
  346|       |        match sender {
  347|       |            Some(sender) => match sender.try_send((bytes, brokered)) {
  348|       |                Ok(()) => TB_OK,
  349|       |                Err(mpsc::error::TrySendError::Full(_)) => TB_BACKPRESSURE,
  350|       |                Err(mpsc::error::TrySendError::Closed(_)) => TB_CLOSED,
  351|       |            },
  352|       |            None => TB_CLOSED,
  353|       |        }
  354|       |    })) {
  355|       |        Ok(code) => code,
  356|       |        Err(_) => TB_PANICKED,
  357|       |    }
  358|       |}
  359|       |
  360|       |unsafe extern "C" fn shutdown(ctx: *mut c_void, deadline_ms: u64) -> i32 {
  361|       |    match catch_unwind(AssertUnwindSafe(|| {
  362|       |        if ctx.is_null() {
  363|       |            return TB_BAD_ARGUMENT;
  364|       |        }
  365|       |        let state = unsafe { &*(ctx.cast::<RuntimeState>()) };
  366|       |        state.inbound.lock().expect("module inbound lock").take();
  367|       |        match state.runtime.lock().expect("module runtime lock").take() {
  368|       |            Some(runtime) => {
  369|       |                runtime.shutdown_timeout(Duration::from_millis(deadline_ms));
  370|       |                TB_OK
  371|       |            }
  372|       |            None => TB_CLOSED,
  373|       |        }
  374|       |    })) {
  375|       |        Ok(code) => code,
  376|       |        Err(_) => TB_PANICKED,
  377|       |    }
  378|       |}

  419|       |            out.cast::<TbModuleVtableV1Prefix>()

  423|       |                    module_ctx: state,

  431|       |/// Initialize the module runtime and start its async setup function.
  432|       |///
  433|       |/// This is public only for [`module_export!`] expansions. Module authors call
  434|       |/// the macro, not this function directly.
  435|       |///
  436|       |/// # Safety
  437|       |/// The host vtable must meet [`TbHostVtable::read_compatible`]'s requirements.
  438|       |/// A non-null `out` must be aligned and writable for its declared capacity,
  439|       |/// with a readable size field; writes are bounded to that capacity. Borrowed
  440|       |/// configuration bytes must remain readable during initialization.
  441|       |/// In particular an affirmative routing callback is a trusted host assertion
  442|       |/// that only real broker deliveries enter `deliver`, not an arbitrary frame
  443|       |/// injection capability. Artifact attestation does not establish this fact.

  451|       |) -> i32

  454|       |    Fut: Future<Output = Result<()>> + Send + 'static,
  455|       |{
  456|       |    unsafe {
  457|       |        start_module_runtime(
  458|       |            host,
  459|       |            out,
  460|       |            worker_threads,
  461|       |            detach_on_panic,
  462|       |            setup,
  463|       |            None,
  464|       |            false,
  465|       |        )
  466|       |    }

  482|       |where
  483|       |    F: FnOnce(Connection) -> Fut + Send + 'static,
  484|       |    Fut: Future<Output = Result<()>> + Send + 'static,
  485|       |{
  486|       |    unsafe {
  487|       |        start_module_runtime(
  488|       |            host,
  489|       |            out,
  490|       |            worker_threads,
  491|       |            detach_on_panic,
  492|       |            setup,
  493|       |            None,
  494|       |            true,
  495|       |        )
  496|       |    }

  498|       |
  499|       |unsafe fn start_module_runtime<F, Fut>(
  500|       |    host: *const TbHostVtable,
  501|       |    out: *mut TbModuleVtable,
  502|       |    worker_threads: usize,
  503|       |    detach_on_panic: bool,
  504|       |    setup: F,
  505|       |    reinitialize_factory: Option<ReinitializeFactory>,
  506|       |    linked: bool,
  507|       |) -> i32
  508|       |where
  509|       |    F: FnOnce(Connection) -> Fut + Send + 'static,
  510|       |    Fut: Future<Output = Result<()>> + Send + 'static,
  511|       |{
  512|       |    match catch_unwind(AssertUnwindSafe(|| {
  513|       |        if host.is_null() || out.is_null() || worker_threads == 0 {
  514|       |            return TB_BAD_ARGUMENT;
  515|       |        }
  516|       |        // `out.size` is input as well as output: an older ABI-v1 host owns a
  517|       |        // shorter allocation. Read only the frozen first field until its
  518|       |        // capacity is known, then write no further than that boundary.
  519|       |        let out_capacity = unsafe { out.cast::<u32>().read() };
  520|       |        if out_capacity < TB_MODULE_VTABLE_BASE_SIZE {
  521|       |            return TB_BAD_ARGUMENT;
  522|       |        }
  523|       |        // `size` is the frozen prefix field; do not copy the full vtable until
  524|       |        // the host has proved that all v1 fields are present.
  525|       |        let Some(host) = (unsafe { TbHostVtable::read_compatible(host) }) else {
  526|       |            return TB_BAD_ARGUMENT;
  527|       |        };
  528|       |        let host = HostCalls(host);
  529|       |
  530|       |        // A cdylib carries its own statically linked `tracing` and `std` state;
  531|       |        // this registration is global to the module's copy, not the embedding
  532|       |        // host's. Failure therefore means this module runtime was initialized
  533|       |        // more than once and cannot safely replace the existing subscriber.
  534|       |        if !linked
  535|       |            && tracing::subscriber::set_global_default(HostSubscriber {
  536|       |                host,
  537|       |                next_span: AtomicU64::new(1),
  538|       |                max_level: tracing::level_filters::LevelFilter::TRACE,
  539|       |            })
  540|       |            .is_err()
  541|       |        {
  542|       |            return TB_CLOSED;
  543|       |        }
  544|       |
  545|       |        let panic_host = host;
  546|       |        let panic_location = std::sync::Arc::new(StdMutex::new(None::<String>));
  547|       |        let hook_location = panic_location.clone();
  548|       |        if !linked {
  549|       |            std::panic::set_hook(Box::new(move |panic| {
  550|       |                let location = panic.location().map_or_else(
  551|       |                    || "module panicked at an unknown location".to_string(),
  552|       |                    |location| {
  553|       |                        let file = std::path::Path::new(location.file())
  554|       |                            .file_name()
  555|       |                            .and_then(|file| file.to_str())
  556|       |                            .unwrap_or("module");
  557|       |                        format!(
  558|       |                            "module panicked at {}:{}:{}",
  559|       |                            file,
  560|       |                            location.line(),
  561|       |                            location.column()
  562|       |                        )
  563|       |                    },
  564|       |                );
  565|       |                // The payload is intentionally neither formatted nor forwarded:
  566|       |                // it may contain arguments, credentials, or recovery material.
  567|       |                *hook_location.lock().expect("panic location lock") = Some(location.clone());
  568|       |                panic_host.log(1, location.as_bytes());
  569|       |            }));
  570|       |        }
  571|       |
  572|       |        let runtime = match tokio::runtime::Builder::new_multi_thread()
  573|       |            .worker_threads(worker_threads)
  574|       |            .enable_all()
  575|       |            .build()
  576|       |        {
  577|       |            Ok(runtime) => runtime,
  578|       |            Err(_) => return TB_CLOSED,
  579|       |        };
  580|       |        let (inbound_tx, inbound_rx) = mpsc::channel(MODULE_QUEUE_CAPACITY);
  581|       |        let transport = Arc::new(ModuleTransport {
  582|       |            host,
  583|       |            inbound: Mutex::new(inbound_rx),
  584|       |            provenance: Arc::new(AtomicBool::new(false)),
  585|       |            detach_on_panic,
  586|       |        });
  587|       |        let connection_slot = Arc::new(StdMutex::new(None));
  588|       |        let task_connection_slot = connection_slot.clone();
  589|       |
  590|       |        runtime.spawn(async move {
  591|       |            let connection = module_connection(transport);
  592|       |            let outcome = match connection.handshake().await.map(|()| connection) {
  593|       |                Ok(connection) => {
  594|       |                    connection.__set_panic_handler(std::sync::Arc::new(move || {
  595|       |                        let location = panic_location
  596|       |                            .lock()
  597|       |                            .expect("panic location lock")
  598|       |                            .take()
  599|       |                            .unwrap_or_else(|| "an unknown location".to_string());
  600|       |                        Error::MethodFailed {
  601|       |                            name: MODULE_PANIC_ERROR.to_string(),
  602|       |                            message: format!("a module method panicked at {location}"),
  603|       |                        }
  604|       |                    }));
  605|       |                    match setup(connection.clone()).await {
  606|       |                        Ok(()) => {
  607|       |                            *task_connection_slot.lock().expect("module connection lock") =
  608|       |                                Some(connection.clone());
  609|       |                            host.ready();
  610|       |                            // Keep the connection (and therefore the served
  611|       |                            // object tree and transport) alive until shutdown
  612|       |                            // stops this runtime. Setup returning means ready,
  613|       |                            // not that the module has finished serving.
  614|       |                            std::future::pending::<()>().await;
  615|       |                            Ok(())
  616|       |                        }
  617|       |                        Err(error) => Err(error),
  618|       |                    }
  619|       |                }
  620|       |                Err(error) => Err(error),
  621|       |            };
  622|       |            if let Err(error) = outcome {
  623|       |                tracing::error!(error = %error, "tinybus module failed");
  624|       |                host.fault();
  625|       |            }
  626|       |        });
  627|       |
  628|       |        let reinitializer =
  629|       |            reinitialize_factory.map(|factory| factory(runtime.handle().clone(), connection_slot));
  630|       |        let supports_reinitialize = reinitializer.is_some();
  631|       |
  632|       |        let state = Box::new(RuntimeState {
  633|       |            host,
  634|       |            inbound: StdMutex::new(Some(inbound_tx)),
  635|       |            runtime: StdMutex::new(Some(runtime)),
  636|       |            reinitialize: reinitializer,
  637|       |        });
  638|       |        let state = Box::into_raw(state).cast::<c_void>();
  639|       |        unsafe { write_module_vtable(out, out_capacity, state, supports_reinitialize) };
  640|       |        TB_OK
  641|       |    })) {
  642|       |        Ok(code) => code,
  643|       |        Err(_) => TB_PANICKED,
  644|       |    }
  645|       |}
  646|       |
  647|       |unsafe fn parse_config<C: serde::de::DeserializeOwned>(
  648|       |    host: *const TbHostVtable,
  649|       |) -> std::result::Result<C, i32> {
  650|       |    if host.is_null() {
  651|       |        return Err(TB_BAD_ARGUMENT);
  652|       |    }
  653|       |    let host_ref = unsafe { TbHostVtable::read_compatible(host) }.ok_or(TB_BAD_ARGUMENT)?;
  654|       |    if host_ref.config.len > 1024 * 1024
  655|       |        || (host_ref.config.ptr.is_null() && host_ref.config.len != 0)
  656|       |    {
  657|       |        return Err(TB_BAD_ARGUMENT);
  658|       |    }
  659|       |    let bytes = if host_ref.config.len == 0 {
  660|       |        b"{}".as_slice()
  661|       |    } else {
  662|       |        unsafe { std::slice::from_raw_parts(host_ref.config.ptr, host_ref.config.len) }
  663|       |    };
  664|       |    serde_json::from_slice::<C>(bytes).map_err(|_| TB_BAD_ARGUMENT)
  665|       |}

  730|       |///
  731|       |/// # Safety
  732|       |/// The caller must uphold the host, output, configuration, and routing contracts
  733|       |/// of [`start_module`].
  734|       |#[doc(hidden)]
  735|       |pub unsafe fn start_linked_reconfigurable_module<C, F, Fut>(
  736|       |    host: *const TbHostVtable,
  737|       |    out: *mut TbModuleVtable,
  738|       |    worker_threads: usize,
  739|       |    detach_on_panic: bool,
  740|       |    setup: F,
  741|       |) -> i32
  742|       |where
  743|       |    C: serde::de::DeserializeOwned + Send + 'static,
  744|       |    F: Fn(Connection, C) -> Fut + Clone + Send + Sync + 'static,
  745|       |    Fut: Future<Output = Result<()>> + Send + 'static,
  746|       |{
  747|       |    unsafe {
  748|       |        start_reconfigurable_module_mode(host, out, worker_threads, detach_on_panic, setup, true)
  749|       |    }
  750|       |}
  751|       |
  752|       |unsafe fn start_reconfigurable_module_mode<C, F, Fut>(
  753|       |    host: *const TbHostVtable,
  754|       |    out: *mut TbModuleVtable,
  755|       |    worker_threads: usize,
  756|       |    detach_on_panic: bool,
  757|       |    setup: F,
  758|       |    linked: bool,
  759|       |) -> i32
  760|       |where
  761|       |    C: serde::de::DeserializeOwned + Send + 'static,
  762|       |    F: Fn(Connection, C) -> Fut + Clone + Send + Sync + 'static,
  763|       |    Fut: Future<Output = Result<()>> + Send + 'static,
  764|       |{
  765|       |    let parsed = catch_unwind(AssertUnwindSafe(|| unsafe { parse_config::<C>(host) }));
  766|       |    let config = match parsed {
  767|       |        Ok(Ok(config)) => config,
  768|       |        Ok(Err(code)) => return code,
  769|       |        Err(_) => return TB_PANICKED,
  770|       |    };
  771|       |    let initial_setup = setup.clone();
  772|       |    let reinitialize_factory: ReinitializeFactory = Box::new(move |handle, connection_slot| {
  773|       |        let reinitialize_lock = StdMutex::new(());
  774|       |        Box::new(move |ptr, len| {
  775|       |            // Setup mutates the module's live object tree. Serializing retries
  776|       |            // keeps two operators from interleaving partial configurations.
  777|       |            let _guard = reinitialize_lock.lock().expect("module reinitialize lock");
  778|       |            let bytes = if len == 0 {
  779|       |                b"{}".as_slice()
  780|       |            } else {
  781|       |                // SAFETY: the ABI callback validates this borrowed slice and
  782|       |                // keeps it alive for the duration of this call.
  783|       |                unsafe { std::slice::from_raw_parts(ptr, len) }
  784|       |            };
  785|       |            let Ok(config) = serde_json::from_slice::<C>(bytes) else {
  786|       |                return TB_BAD_ARGUMENT;
  787|       |            };
  788|       |            let Some(connection) = connection_slot
  789|       |                .lock()
  790|       |                .expect("module connection lock")
  791|       |                .clone()
  792|       |            else {
  793|       |                return TB_CLOSED;
  794|       |            };
  795|       |            match handle.block_on(async {
  796|       |                tokio::time::timeout(MODULE_REINITIALIZE_DEADLINE, setup(connection, config)).await
  797|       |            }) {
  798|       |                Ok(Ok(())) => TB_OK,
  799|       |                Ok(Err(_)) => TB_CLOSED,
  800|       |                Err(_) => TB_TIMEOUT,
  801|       |            }
  802|       |        })
  803|       |    });
  804|       |    unsafe {
  805|       |        start_module_runtime(
  806|       |            host,
  807|       |            out,
  808|       |            worker_threads,
  809|       |            detach_on_panic,
  810|       |            move |connection| initial_setup(connection, config),
  811|       |            Some(reinitialize_factory),
  812|       |            linked,
  813|       |        )
  814|       |    }
  815|       |}

  982|       |/// Generate Rust-addressable entry points for linking several modules into a
  983|       |/// single executable. The entry points have no shared C linker symbol names.
  984|       |#[macro_export]
  985|       |macro_rules! module_export_static {
  986|       |    (setup = $setup:path, config = $config:ty, $($rest:tt)*) => {
  987|       |        $crate::module_export! {
  988|       |            @configured export = {},
  989|       |            start = $crate::start_linked_reconfigurable_module,
  990|       |            setup = $setup,
  991|       |            config = $config,
  992|       |            $($rest)*
  993|       |        }
  994|       |        $crate::module_export! { @linked }
  995|       |    };
  996|       |    (setup = $setup:path, $($rest:tt)*) => {
  997|       |        $crate::module_export! {
  998|       |            @plain export = {},
  999|       |            start = $crate::start_linked_module,
 1000|       |            setup = $setup,
 1001|       |            $($rest)*
 1002|       |        }
 1003|       |        $crate::module_export! { @linked }
 1004|       |    };
 1005|       |}

 1007|       |/// Select the dynamic or linked export from one declaration.
 1008|       |///
 1009|       |/// The consuming crate declares a `static-link` feature. Its default build
 1010|       |/// retains the C exports, while the linked build uses Rust-addressable entry
 1011|       |/// points and the linked runtime mode.
 1012|       |#[macro_export]
 1013|       |macro_rules! module_export_optional_static {
 1014|       |    ($($declaration:tt)*) => {
 1015|       |        #[cfg(not(feature = "static-link"))]
 1016|       |        $crate::module_export! { $($declaration)* }
 1017|       |        #[cfg(feature = "static-link")]
 1018|       |        $crate::module_export_static! { $($declaration)* }
 1019|       |    };
